title: Spark Execution Basics
learningOutcome: Trace Spark execution from SparkSession + config through lazy transforms to the action that creates Jobs, Stages, Tasks, and Executors

questions.prompt: Look at the right-hand code. What does `SparkSession.builder…getOrCreate()` create?
choices: Only a temporary local Python object with no cluster meaning
The Spark application entrypoint (driver) used to build jobs
One executor process per config line
questions.correctAnswer: The Spark application entrypoint (driver) used to build jobs
questions.explanation: SparkSession is the driver-side entrypoint. Your main() runs on the driver; the session is how you submit work to the cluster.

questions.prompt: Where does `.appName("acme-filter-revenue-v1")` show up after the job finishes?
choices: As the application name in Spark History Server / UI
As a Parquet column in OUTPUT_PATH
It is ignored unless you also set spark.sql.shuffle.partitions
questions.correctAnswer: As the application name in Spark History Server / UI
questions.explanation: appName labels the application in the Spark UI / History Server so you can find this run among others.

questions.prompt: What worker resources does this job ask the cluster for?
questions.explanation: When the session is built, this app requests 2 executors with 1 core and 1g memory each (instances / cores / memory). That is the cluster footprint for running tasks.

questions.prompt: Who runs the `main()` function and builds the execution plan?
questions.explanation: Application code runs on the driver. Executors run distributed tasks after an action.

questions.prompt: In the code, which of these is a transformation (lazy — does not start a Job by itself)?
questions.explanation: filter and withColumn are transformations that extend lineage without executing yet.

questions.prompt: After `filter` and `withColumn`, why hasn’t Spark finished writing the output yet?
choices: Because OUTPUT_PATH is invalid until History Server opens
Because transformations are lazy — nothing runs until an action
Because appName must be unique per write
questions.correctAnswer: Because transformations are lazy — nothing runs until an action
questions.explanation: Spark records how to compute the result and waits for an action before scheduling work.

questions.prompt: Which line in the exhibit is the action that triggers cluster execution?
questions.explanation: Writing Parquet is an action — that launches Job(s).

questions.prompt: If someone inserted `valid.count()` between the filter and the write, how many Jobs would you expect?
choices: 2 Jobs — count and write are both actions
questions.correctAnswer: 2 Jobs — count and write are both actions
questions.explanation: Each action typically triggers its own Job.

questions.prompt: Open History Server for this app → Jobs. With only the write action (as in the code), how many Jobs should you see?
questions.explanation: One write action → one Job for this narrow pipeline.

questions.prompt: Match the hierarchy Spark uses after an action runs:
choices: Task → contains Stages → each Stage is a Job
Job → Stages → Tasks (tasks run on executors)
Executor → creates Jobs → each Job is one Python line
appName → creates one Task per config key
questions.correctAnswer: Job → Stages → Tasks (tasks run on executors)
questions.explanation: Action → Job → Stages → Tasks on executors.
